scope.question: How much of the prospective next-token benefit of reusing the previous minibatch gradient requires the correct context-target assignment?
scope.estimand: On one true-target online trajectory, the packet-weighted next-token NLL difference between an equal-radius previous true-gradient branch and the mean of four previous target-permuted branches from the same center.
not_claimed: different permutation RNG states are independent model trajectories
token IDs may be permuted into conditioning positions
equal-radius raw-gradient branches are counterfactual AdamW optimizer steps
a one-step audit establishes long-horizon language-model quality
the CPU smoke is paper evidence

model.acquisition: external offline snapshot; local_files_only is mandatory

dataset.license_filter: per-record CC BY or CC BY-SA only
dataset.acquisition: external offline snapshot authenticated as one content-addressed tree

optimization.counterfactual_direction: stored raw minibatch gradient; no AdamW moments, preconditioner, or weight decay are applied to virtual branches
optimization.reuse_endpoint_radius: median realized norm of the last 16 true-target AdamW updates

audit.permutation_unit: predicted next-token targets within the previous chronological packet

branches.K4: mean outcome of four equal-radius previous target-permuted gradients

audit.live_update: exactly one true-target AdamW update after all branches and permutation gradients are computed

reporting.inference: paired circular block intervals for K1-vs-K0, K4-vs-K0, and K1-vs-K4 NLL/top-1/top-5 contrasts; four permutation replicas are nested and averaged within packet
reporting.permutation_sensitivity: nested K-prefix summaries at K=1,2,4 plus outcome-level finite-permutation Monte Carlo standard errors
reporting.perplexity_inference: perplexity is exp(aggregate NLL); interval claims remain on the additive NLL scale
